statement: A scoring signal that checks a config key by presence alone, not content, credits an auto-generated placeholder identically to a real implementation — npm writes "test": "echo \"Error: no test specified\" && exit 1" into every npm init package.json, and a presence check scored it the same as a real test runner. Separately, two criteria deriving a verdict from the same underlying fact through independently maintained branches diverged on identical input: one credited a package's lint/typecheck scripts, the other zeroed them under a different code path, reaching opposite conclusions about the same repository. Require content matching wherever a key has a common auto-generated placeholder, and thread one shared computation into every consumer of the same fact instead of letting duplicate logic drift apart.

A detector that matches only one documented form of an artifact treats every other valid form as absent — this one recognized pull_request_template.md but not GitHub's directory form (.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/<name>.md), reporting a repo using the directory form as having no template at all. Separately, a doc that restates a version as hand-written prose drifts from the code constant it describes: docs/format-stability.md said reportFormatVersion was 1.0 after the code had moved to 1.1, understating what the tool actually emits on the very page an external gate binds to. Enumerate every documented form a detector claims to cover, and guard any hand-restated version string against its source-of-truth constant.
